newsitem.title: USA: Chicago alderman says broke no ethics rules - papers.
newsitem.headline: Chicago alderman says broke no ethics rules - papers.

text.p: Chicago Alderman Edward Burke said Thursday he breached no legal ethics in representing clients on property tax appeals while serving as chairman of the City Council finance committee, Chicago newspapers reported Friday.
Burke also told reporters that while he broke no laws, he will no longer participate in city tax challenges in his private practice, the Chicago Sun-Times and Chicago Tribune said.

The tax appeals lawsuits filed by Burke in his private practice at times included arguments that parts of the city's budget and tax levies were technically illegal. As finance chairman, Burke oversees the committee that prepares the city budget, tax questions and approves settlements of legal claims against Chicago.
Burke also said he will require all media inquiries about his business dealings to be made in writing and will respond in writing, the newspapers said.
Burke said he believed reporters had misquoted Mayor Richard Daley last week when they reported that he had said, "It is a very difficult position he is placing everyone in," the Tribune reported.

When asked to respond to Burke's statement later Thursday, Daley said, "I think what I said is he has to answer to himself," the Tribune reported. "I did question anyone who is voting on the budget to sue later on."
